summary.one_line: The bilingual devkit guide remains accurate, and the diary records the test-only Windows CI path correction.

purpose.evidence: Read all 12 changed Markdown paths. New RU/EN devkit pages answer how to obtain and use the published shared development tools; the research-index pair adds the route, related modding pages distinguish command tools from a universal native SDK, and the diary pair records the extraction's process and limits. The page points to the actual heroes5-mod-devkit repository, not a promised future package.

structure.evidence: Both devkit pages proceed from included components to setup, first H5U marker cycle, command-driven battles and extraction checks. Nav and research-index entries link the new pair; native-ui/resource-overrides/test-maps give contextual backlinks. The dated diary entry appends extraction results and the subsequent shadow-import correction without replacing earlier historical observations. specificity.evidence: Compared the new PowerShell setup and H5U cycle against the reviewed devkit README and script parsers: Git clone/venv/requirements, H5_WORKSPACE/H5_GAME_DIR, copying examples/menu-marker, prepare/build/deploy/launch --sandbox and rollback align. game_control parser exposes status, heroes, teleport, interact, confirm, finish --winner 0, results, hero and quit. The public polygon's pack_8 location permits teleport Brem 14 50 before interacting; dispatch alone is not called a completed fight. Included-tool table matches mod-dev, test-map, native-probe, game_control, game-ui and inspect_universe entrypoints.

reproducibility.evidence: The website gives an actionable setup path and an expected visual marker, then links the full SDK command reference. Parent reports 37 SDK tests and 48 legacy bridge tests passing, a fresh clone's 37 tests with no root path variables, and an empty external-workspace staged map with 60 objects/six arenas and valid ZIP. The article says the extracted kit has not had a separate live-game launch; I did not start a game. Parent reports knowledge build/check 8 Node/21 Python/37 HTML passing; All 12 browser tests later passed per parent.

evidence.evidence: The SDK source review at HEAD fcc0422 established canonical shared scripts, workspace separation, optional native artifacts and import-path hardening. The new diary entry preserves the first failed empty-workspace H5M/journal attempt, explains the later successful 60-object/six-arena build, and records the inert shadow-module differential check without claiming game execution. It links the current devkit page and keeps predictor C++ and historical native results separate. I did not independently rerun the SDK suite or examine a game/profile; parent supplied those machine outcomes. Final diary correction matches SDK HEAD 4406cf0: GitHub Windows represented a temporary path with RUNNER~1 while CLI returned its full spelling; the test resolves both paths before equality comparison. The exact SDK diff touched only the test assertion/config base, not runtime tools.

applicability.evidence: The new page targets Windows 10/11, Python 3.10+ x64 and installed Tribes of the East with Universe, and links pinned native build hashes. It says the predictor DLL is excluded, a universal plugin SDK is not provided, complete profile isolation is unproven, EXE startup can briefly take focus, and physical mouse checks differ from addressed input. Test-map and native UI updates say command tools are available while still denying a universal native API.

translations.evidence: Compared both 101-line devkit articles and all five updated RU/EN article pairs: the component table, setup commands, marker cycle, quickbattle commands, 37/48 test counts, 60-object map, no-new-live-launch caveat, shadow-import correction and external SDK link agree. RU/EN nav entries, research-index links and diary histories have counterparts. Reciprocal metadata and local links are covered by parent-reported site checks; this is not a professional translation audit. The SDK remains the canonical code and command reference; website steps are a bounded onboarding route. review:info lists exactly the 12 changed Markdown paths covered here; no source/artifact was edited by this reviewer.
